# Parts Town Leases 538,450-Square-Foot Pendergrass Hub, Adds 140 Jobs

By Marc Washington

Published on September 07, 2026

Approximate Parts Town Business Park Google Street View

Parts Town Unlimited has signed a lease for a sprawling 538,450-square-foot distribution facility in Pendergrass, Georgia, a Jackson County town of roughly 500 residents that will soon host the company's largest global fulfillment center. The facility is expect
highlights:
Parts Town Unlimited has signed a lease for a sprawling 538,450-square-foot distribution facility in Pendergrass, Georgia, a Jackson County town of roughly 500 residents that will soon host the company's largest global fulfillment center. The facility is expected to bring more than 140 team members to the area and is designed to put parts closer to Southeast customers while cutting shipping times and costs.

According to WSB-TV, the warehouse will rely on robotic conveyance and planned AI-powered robotics for packing, shipping and receiving. Parts Town Unlimited signed the full-building lease for Building 1 at Jackson 85 North Business Park, located at 779 Parker Industrial Road, in a deal developed by Trammell Crow Company and joint venture partner CBRE Investment Management, according to Commercial Search. The Class A cross-dock building features 40-foot clear heights, 124 dock doors, four drive-in ramps, 185-foot concrete truck courts, parking for 171 cars and 148 trailers, and a watertight roof already prepped for solar panels, per the same outlet's reporting.
...
The Georgia site will surpass the company's previous largest fulfillment center, a 427,000-square-foot facility in Litchfield Park, Arizona, that opened in December 2024 with an AutoStore system running 85 robots across 60,000 product bins, according to Digital Commerce 360. That Arizona facility was built to handle 4,500 daily orders. Parts Town's distribution network also includes global fulfillment centers in Chicago, Phoenix, and Munich, and the Pendergrass site will be the company's first LEED-certified global fulfillment center, with LEED certification focused on energy efficiency, resource conservation, and healthier indoor environments.

Bill Geary said the new global fulfillment center represents an important next step in the evolution of ... 's North American distribution network, and that it will help serve customers and manufacturer partners with greater speed, flexibility, and scale. The company plans to distribute genuine manufacturer parts for commercial foodservice equipment, residential appliances, and HVAC systems out of the new hub, and expects to move in by the end of
...
Pendergrass sits along Interstate 85 at its intersection with U.S. Highway 129, roughly 60 miles northeast of ... , and has quietly transformed into a regional logistics hub housing facilities ... . Jackson 85 North Business Park itself spans 215 acres, with Phase ... 's building alongside a 1,017,900-square-foot speculative facility, and Phase Two planned to add up to 1.48 million square feet across additional industrial sites, according to Commercial Search.

# FST Logistics Expands Central Ohio Presence with New West Jefferson, Ohio Facility 

Dublin, OH – FST Logistics, a leading third-party logistics provider specializing in temperature-controlled transportation, retail consolidation, warehousing and supply chain solutions, is proud to announce the expansion of its Central Ohio footprint with the opening of a new facility in West Jefferson, Ohio. The new location adds 343,500 square feet of warehouse space to FST’s growing network and strengthens the company’s ability to support customers’ growth throughout the Midwest and beyond. 

The expansion provides additional capacity for FST to support the evolving needs of its customers, while creating opportunities to serve new customers seeking strategic warehousing and distribution solutions in Central Ohio. The facility features 38 dock doors, two drive-in doors, 40-foot clear height, 254 parking spaces and 85 trailer parking spaces, providing the infrastructure and capacity needed to support a wide range of customer operations. 

“Central Ohio continues ... be an important market for FST, and we’re excited to open this ... needs of a large-scale ... and CPG brand. ... long-term ... our employee-owners, ... West Jefferson community ... on the growth ... all three. ... jobs, we ... to come,” said Brad Wright, President of FST Logistics. 

The additional capacity will support FST’s broad range of warehousing and supply chain services, including storage, distribution, retail consolidation and other customized logistics solutions. The facility provides FST with the ability to accommodate customers with varying inventory and distribution requirements while offering a strategic Central Ohio location to support their supply chain operations. 

The facility provides convenient access to major transportation routes and strengthens FST’s ability to serve customers throughout Central Ohio and key national markets. The expansion further enhances FST’s scalable warehousing capabilities while maintaining the company’s commitment to customer service, operational flexibility and supply chain efficiency.

# G10 Fulfillment to Celebrate Grand Opening of New Kenosha Distribution Facility with Ribbon-Cutting Ceremony

 Geneva10 

Sep 01, 2026, 08:34 ET

Mayor and Kenosha County Executive to join company and community leaders in marking the milestone expansion

KENOSHA, Wis., Sept. 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- G10 Fulfillment, a North American third-party logistics and fulfillment provider, will hold a ribbon-cutting ceremony celebrating the grand opening of its new distribution facility in Kenosha, Wisconsin, on Thursday, September 10, 2026, at 11:00 a.m. at 12345 38th Street.

The new 315,000-square-foot facility replaces G10's former Twin Lakes location and more than doubles the company's Midwest warehouse capacity. Positioned along the Chicago–Milwaukee freight corridor, the site supports large-scale order fulfillment and regional inventory distribution as part of G10's broader logistics network.

Local officials will join G10 leadership to mark the occasion. Kenosha Mayor David Bogdala and Kenosha County Executive Samantha Kerkmam will offer remarks, with the Kenosha Area Business Alliance (KABA) serving as emcee for the event. Members of the media are welcome to attend.

"This facility represents a major step forward for our Midwest operations," said Mark Becker, CEO of G10 Fulfillment. "Doubling our capacity here in Kenosha allows us to support our retail partners with faster, more reliable fulfillment, and we're proud to be growing alongside a community that has been such a strong partner to our business."

About G10 Fulfillment

Founded in 2009, G10 Fulfillment has grown from a 10,000-square-foot airplane hangar into a multi-node logistics network across the United States. The company combines fulfillment technology with operational expertise to help retail and e-commerce brands—ranging from Walmart and Amazon to fast-growing Shopify companies—manage inventory, shipping and logistics across every sales channel, including regulated hazmat shipping, with speed, accuracy and consistency. For more information, visit https://g10fulfillment.com/.

highlights:

#### New Kenosha hub significantly expands G10 Fulfillment’s Midwest warehouse capacity

 Posted in Kenosha County Economic Development 

A Delavan-based third-party logistics and fulfillment company has significantly expanded its Midwest warehouse capacity after moving into a new distribution facility in Kenosha.

G10 Fulfillment now occupies 315,000 square feet of a 600,000-square-foot building at 12345 38th St., just off Interstate 94. The move increases G10’s dock capacity to 65 doors from 30.

“The Midwest is probably the most important hub for us,” said co-founder and CEO Mark Becker, who was on hand Thursday for a ribbon-cutting at the facility. He pointed to the region’s freight infrastructure and its location along the trucking corridor between Chicago and Milwaukee.

Becker said the facility can handle nearly 7 acres of inventory under one roof. G10 shares the building with food manufacturer Eagle Foods.

G10 invested about $2 million in the Kenosha buildout, which Becker said covered racking, automation and staffing costs.

The facility has about 100 workers, a figure he expects to reach 150 by March 2027. Seasonal hiring could push employment toward 200 during the Black Friday peak before tapering in January.

#### G10’s real estate

The move consolidates two smaller warehouses — a 150,000-square-foot building in Twin Lakes and a 50,000-square-foot site in New Berlin — into one operation.

G10 is giving up both former buildings rather than keeping them as backup capacity, according to the chief executive. The company owns the Twin Lakes site, which is being leased to Allied Plastics. The New Berlin property is owned by one of Becker’s business partners and is being turned over to another venture.

Kenosha will be one of three anchor hubs in G10’s national network, he said, alongside a Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, warehouse scheduled to open in October and a planned Ontario, Canada, facility targeted for 2027.

The company is also exploring a location in Southern California.

G10 has grown from a 10,000-square-foot hangar in Lake Geneva in 2009 into a fulfillment operation that stores, processes and ships products for manufacturers and brands across multiple sales channels.

# 3PL Arvato opens its seventh logistics facility in Louisville 

400,000 square foot site takes Arvato’s total Louisville footprint beyond four million square feet.

By DC Velocity Staff Oct 05, 2026

DC Velocity Staff See Full Bio 

The supply chain management and e-commerce third party logistics provider (3PL) Arvato has opened its seventh logistics facility in Louisville, Kentucky, saying the move further expands its presence in one of the United States’ most important logistics hubs.

The new, wholly-owned site adds approximately 400,000 square feet of capacity, taking Arvato’s total Louisville footprint beyond four million square feet. Expected to create approximately 150 new jobs, the facility further strengthens the company’s ability to support growing fulfillment and distribution requirements for clients across North America, Arvato said.

According to Germany-based Arvato, brands need supply chain solutions that can support growth without adding complexity, whether they are entering new markets, managing rising order volumes, or optimizing delivery performance.

Its new Louisville facility is a direct response to these changing market requirements, the company said. By expanding its U.S. network, Arvato is providing clients with additional capacity, greater operational agility, and access to a highly connected distribution hub. Located near Louisville International Airport (SDF), the facility enables efficient distribution across major consumer markets and supports faster, more reliable fulfillment operations. It also benefits from late cut-off times, enabling faster direct-to-consumer deliveries and supporting time-critical shipments such as spare parts and critical equipment.

highlights:
Maersk Invests $100 Million in Massachusetts Fulfillment Hub - Supply Chain 24/7

## The new 617,000-square-foot Maersk fulfillment center will open in late August and create about 1,000 jobs

 

Source: Courtesy of Maersk

Maersk is investing $100 million in a new fulfillment center in Hopedale, Massachusetts, creating about 1,000 jobs and expanding Northeast delivery capacity.

 By 24/7 Staff July 16, 2026 

Maersk will open a new 617,000-square-foot fulfillment center in Hopedale, Massachusetts, later this summer, investing $100 million in the project and creating approximately 1,000 jobs.

The facility will become part of Maersk's North American contract logistics network and will work with a major e-commerce customer. At full capacity, the site is expected to process up to 330,000 units a day while expanding the company's fulfillment and delivery network across the Northeast.

The Hopedale facility marks one of Maersk's larger recent investments in U.S. logistics infrastructure as retailers and brands continue placing inventory closer to customers to speed deliveries.

“We are seeing continued customer demand for modern fulfillment capabilities,” said Dave Hune, Head of Maersk Contract Logistics North America. “Our investment in Hopedale reflects continued customer demand for modern fulfillment capabilities and reinforces Maersk's commitment to building resilient, scalable supply chains across North America.”

## Built for high-volume e-commerce

The fulfillment center is equipped with automated conveyor and sortation systems designed to handle large volumes of orders. Maersk said the operation will process up to 330,000 units per day during peak periods.

The site will serve a single large-scale e-commerce customer, although Maersk did not identify the company.

Hiring is already underway for leadership, warehouse, and support positions ahead of the facility's opening later this summer.

## Expanding Maersk's Northeast network

The new operation expands Maersk's contract logistics network in North America and strengthens its presence in the Northeast.

The company said many customers are looking to position inventory closer to consumers to reduce delivery times while improving order fulfillment.

The Hopedale facility combines warehousing, fulfillment, and distribution within Maersk's broader logistics network, which includes ocean shipping, trucking, air freight, and inland transportation.

The company said the investment will help it keep up with customer growth while expanding its fulfillment network in one of the country's largest consumer markets.

# Walmart Opens Next-Generation Fulfillment Center in Stockton, Expanding Faster Delivery Across the West Coast

Oct. 8, 2026

 

## New facility will create 1,000+ jobs and use advanced automation and technology to increase fulfillment capacity

STOCKTON, Calif., Oct. 8, 2026 — Walmart today opened its fifth next-generation fulfillment center, a more than 900,000-square-foot facility i
highlights:
Walmart Opens Next-Generation Fulfillment Center in Stockton, Expanding Faster Delivery Across the West Coast
...
STOCKTON, Calif., Oct. 8, 2026 — Walmart today opened its fifth next-generation fulfillment center, a more than 900,000-square-foot facility in Stockton that will create more than 1,000 jobs and expand the retailer’s ability to provide faster shipping and delivery to customers across California and the West Coast.

The new facility represents the latest step in Walmart’s transformation of its supply chain, bringing associates together with advanced automation, technology and machine learning to move products faster and more efficiently. The technology enables Walmart to materially improve storage capacity and increase the number of customer orders the facility can fulfill each day compared with a traditional fulfillment center.

Strategically located in California’s Central Valley, the Stockton facility adds significant fulfillment capacity closer to West Coast customers, helping Walmart expand faster shipping options on millions of items while strengthening its broader store and fulfillment network.
...
“Stockton represents what we mean when we say Walmart is people-led and tech-powered,” said Karisa Sprague, senior vice president, Fulfillment Operations, Walmart U.S. “We’re bringing together associates with advanced technology and automation to create a safer, more efficient operation that can fulfill more orders and get products to customers faster. This facility is an important investment in the Central Valley and a critical part of how we’re building the next generation of Walmart’s fulfillment network across the West Coast.”
...
Combined with the rest of Walmart’s fulfillment network, these next-generation fulfillment centers will enable the retailer to reach 95% of the U.S. population with next- or two-day shipping. Walmart Fulfillment Services, Walmart’s end-to-end third-party fulfillment service, will also leverage the space to fulfill third-party Marketplace items.

JENKINS TOWNSHIP, PA, UNITED STATES, October 7, 2026 / EINPresswire.com/ -- Davinci Micro Fulfillment, which operates a distributed network of “micro site” fulfillment centers providing end to end order, inventory and shipping management for eCommerce sellers, has opened its sixth U.S. facility in Pennsylvania’s Jenkins Township.

Located in Luzerne County, at 141 Commonwealth Drive in CenterPoint Commerce & Trade Park South, the leased facility has 36,231 square feet of space and is purpose designed with equipment, resources and technology to support fulfillment of consumer brands marketed through eCommerce channels including Amazon, Walmart, TikTok and direct-to-consumer platforms.

Founded in 2020, Davinci forward-positions client inventory in smaller fulfillment centers close to consumers to accelerate delivery and reduce shipping costs. The company’s solution incorporates strategically sited warehousing facilities, skilled personnel and a portfolio of AI-enabled technology tools.
...
“Jenkins Township becomes the sixth micro-fulfillment warehouse in our U.S. network. It provided the ideal site and a modern facility to enable us to expand our eCommerce order fulfillment coverage further throughout the Northeast U.S.,” noted Corey Apirian, Davinci’s founder and chief executive. “By enabling consumer brands to forward stage products closer to the consumer, we are helping them keep their brand promise through accurate, fast, cost-efficient order fulfillment that delights the customer and keeps them coming back.” 

Apirian says the new Jenkins Township location will initially employ 10 people, with expectations of growth to 15 employees by the end of the year as new clients are signed and onboarded into the facility.

# Arvato opens seventh Louisville facility, strength­ening its presence in key U.S. logistics hub 

As brands continue to expand across North America, many face increasing challenges in scaling their supply chains quickly, maintaining service levels and building resilience in an increasingly complex market environment. To help clients address these challenges, Ar
highlights:
Arvato opens seventh Louisville facility, strength­ening its presence in key U.S. logistics hub – 

 Press release| October 05, 2026
...
As brands continue to expand across North America, many face increasing challenges in scaling their supply chains quickly, maintaining service levels and building resilience in an increasingly complex market environment. To help clients address these challenges, Arvato has opened its seventh logistics facility in Louisville, Kentucky, further expanding its presence in one of the United States’ most important logistics hubs. The new, wholly-owned site adds approximately 400,000 square feet of capacity, taking Arvato’s total Louisville footprint beyond four million square feet. Expected to create approximately 150 new jobs, the facility further strengthens Arvato’s ability to support growing fulfillment and distribution requirements for clients across North America.
...
The new Louisville facility is a direct response to these changing market requirements. By expanding its U.S. network, Arvato is providing clients with additional capacity, greater operational agility and access to a highly connected distribution hub. Located near Louisville International Airport (SDF), the facility enables efficient distribution across major consumer markets and supports faster, more reliable fulfillment operations. It also benefits from late cut-off times, enabling faster direct-to-consumer deliveries and supporting time-critical shipments such as spare parts and critical equipment.

"Flexibility is often what our clients’ need most. They are looking for partners that can support their growth ambitions across North America while helping them navigate increasingly complex supply chain requirements," says Andreas Podwojewski, Managing Director North America at Arvato. “As we expand our Louisville footprint to seven facilities, we are further strengthening our network and creating the scalability, flexibility and operational excellence our clients need to succeed in a dynamic market environment.”
...
The facility is part of Arvato's continued expansion strategy in Kentucky, where the company has steadily increased capacity since establishing operations in the state in 2005. Today, Arvato operates more than 4 million square feet in Louisville and more than 9 million square feet across the United States. By further strengthening Arvato’s presence in Kentucky, the company is also contributing to the region’s continued economic growth. It also offers significant future expansion opportunities, creating a platform that can continue to grow alongside client requirements for years to come.
